The Nasarawa State Police Command has directed political parties to submit written applications at least 10 days before holding campaigns and rallies ahead of the 2027 general elections. The command also warned political parties and their supporters against political violence, hate speech, cyberbullying, inflammatory propaganda, and the destruction of campaign billboards and posters. According to a statement made available to journalists on Friday, the Police Public Relations Officer in the state, Ramhan Nansel, said the Commissioner of Police, Danko Muhammad, issued the directive during a meeting with political party chairmen, executives, directors-general of campaign organisations, youth and women leaders, and media representatives in Lafia. Nansel stated that the meeting, held at the command headquarters in Lafia, was part of efforts to ensure peaceful and orderly political campaigns, rallies, and elections across the state. He disclosed that Muhammad emphasised the need for political parties to comply strictly with electoral laws, guidelines issued by the Independent National Electoral Commission, and other relevant statutes governing political activities. Kaduna seeks clerics’ support for APC Police invite three over viral video of armed thugs in Kebbi INEC mobilises Edo voters for mock accreditation “The meeting also provided an opportunity for party representatives to seek clarification on political activities, security arrangements, and their responsibilities in ensuring a peaceful electoral process,” he said. The PPRO noted that the parties unanimously pledged to abide by the police directives and conduct themselves peacefully and responsibly in accordance with the law before, during, and after the elections. “Muhammad reiterated the command’s commitment to providing a level playing field for all political parties, adding that the police would remain professional, impartial, and firm in dealing with individuals or groups whose actions threaten public peace and security. “He also urged political party leaders to caution their supporters against violence, intimidation, hate speech, destruction of campaign materials, and other conduct capable of undermining the democratic process,” the statement added. According to the PPRO, the commissioner called on political stakeholders to prioritise dialogue, tolerance, and mutual respect in the interest of peace and stability in the state. He assured residents that the command will work closely with INEC, political parties, other security agencies, and relevant stakeholders to ensure a peaceful and secure electoral process.
